summary: Describes a model for managing virtual terminals, which lets different kinds of terminals and workstations talk to remote systems in a common way. It was prepared for the Defense Communications Agency by MITRE.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 782 proposes a model in which virtual terminals provide a common representation for different real devices. Adaptation units translate between each device and the virtual terminal, while a workstation manages the user's sessions and display.

subtitle: A work-in-progress model for sharing virtual terminals across workstations and devices.

tldr.problem: Different real terminals and workstations have different architectures, while users may need several conversations and devices in one environment.
tldr.mechanism: The VTM model uses virtual terminals as common representations and adaptation units to map between the virtual domain and physical devices.
tldr.outcome: The memo presents an overview and data structures for a model whose operations and control mechanisms were less complete and still under development.

today: RFC 782 describes work in progress and says a minimal implementation was planned to validate the model. It presents an example of possible virtual-terminal mechanisms.

sections.title: A Common View of Different Terminals
sections.content:
The memo describes virtual terminal protocols as a way to provide device-independent, bidirectional, 8-bit byte-oriented communication. A virtual terminal gives communicating entities a common representation rather than exposing each site's device-specific codes.

The document presents its model as work in progress. It says the data structures and addressing functions were more complete than the operations and control mechanisms.
sections.plainLanguage: A virtual terminal gives different devices a shared way to represent input and output. The memo presents a model for that idea rather than a finished protocol.

sections.title: Virtual Terminals and Adaptation Units
sections.content:
The model has cooperating virtual terminals, adaptation units, and workstations. An adaptation unit maps between a real device's workspace and a virtual terminal's workspace, translating user input into virtual commands.

A virtual terminal includes virtual keys, a virtual controller, and a virtual display. The memo identifies stream, line, logical page, physical page, and graphics classes.
sections.plainLanguage: The adaptation unit translates between a real device and the virtual terminal. The virtual terminal organizes input, session control, and display data.

sections.title: Workstation Sessions and Displays
sections.content:
A workstation may manage multiple virtual terminal instances, each associated with a logical terminal display. The user can switch which logical terminal receives input and can map different logical displays onto areas of a physical display.

The model also describes virtual display windows that let an adaptation unit view part of a larger display, with scrolling or access to past activity when the display has file extension.
sections.plainLanguage: A workstation can manage several conversations and switch which one receives the keyboard. Each terminal view can show a selected part of a virtual display.

sections.title: Scope and State of the Work
sections.content:
The RFC provides an overview of the VTM model and a detailed design description of data structures and addressing functions. It says operations and control mechanisms were less complete.

The authors planned an initial minimal implementation to validate the model and submitted the document as an example of mechanisms a virtual terminal should support.
sections.plainLanguage: The data structures were described in detail, but some operations still needed work. The authors planned a minimal implementation to test the model.
